row.evidence: Trello's pricing page lists Enterprise at $17.50/user/month billed annually and says 'This plan includes Atlassian Guard Standard', with 'Free SSO and user provisioning with Atlassian Guard'.
row.notes: Still gated, but the price changed: Enterprise now includes Atlassian Guard Standard at no extra cost, so SCIM costs $17.50/u/mo vs June's $21.50 (Enterprise + ~$4 Guard). Multiplier 3.5 (was 4.3). The pricing page comparison table still says Guard is a separate subscription from $4/month/user. June's 50-seat minimum is not on the current pricing page, so it is dropped. SCIM is Atlassian's org-level SCIM 2.0 (api.atlassian.com/scim/directory/{id}); it creates Atlassian accounts with free Trello access, and an Enterprise license is only granted when an admin adds the user to an Enterprise Workspace. Trello's own SCIM API is being retired, and Trello-only orgs must ask support to fully enable SCIM. SCIM keys expire after one year. JumpCloud and OneLogin come from Atlassian's own guide list.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.price_text: $17.50 per user/month billed annually ($210 per user per year); includes Atlassian Guard Standard

auth.token_source: Atlassian Administration > organization > Security > Identity providers > directory > User provisioning (SCIM base URL and API key)
auth.notes: Token source path paraphrased from the Atlassian configure page; the OpenAPI file also declares an OAuth client-credentials scheme.

deprovision.data_retained: DELETE or IdP removal deactivates the Atlassian account rather than deleting it; deactivated users can be reactivated in Atlassian Administration.

custom.how: Only the Atlassian extension urn:scim:schemas:extension:atlassian-external:1.0 (atlassianAccountId) is defined; no customer-defined attributes.

attributes.notes: Attribute list read from the ScimUser, ScimUserName, EnterpriseUserExtension and ScimGroup schemas in the OpenAPI file; IdP-updatable attributes per the support page.

roles.how: Group-to-app-access mapping: synced groups are assigned to apps and admin roles in Atlassian Administration; a Trello Enterprise license is granted by inviting the user to an Enterprise Workspace.

limitations.text: SCIM provisions Atlassian accounts, not Trello seats: provisioned users get a free managed Trello account and no Enterprise license until an admin grants one (for most organizations).
Trello's own SCIM API is being retired; provisioning goes through the Atlassian organization SCIM API.
Trello-only organizations must contact Atlassian support to fully enable SCIM.
SCIM API keys expire one year after creation.
Atlassian pages disagree on whether group sync works for Trello (see conflicts).

endpoints.purpose: Deactivate a member of an Enterprise (not for AdminHub-managed enterprises)
Grant or revoke an Enterprise license
Make a member an Enterprise admin
Update a Workspace's members (invite by email)
Remove a member from a Workspace
Deactivate or reactivate a Workspace member

limitations.text: Enterprise member deactivation and admin endpoints are unavailable for enterprises that moved user management to Atlassian Administration (AdminHub).

user_api.notes: Trello REST API is usable on every plan; enterprise-member endpoints need an Enterprise. Atlassian's organization admin API is a separate product not researched here.

okta.notes: 'Atlassian Cloud' OIN app markup checks SAML, SWA, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push, Group Linking. Separate 'Trello' OIN app checks SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate and describes SSO and JIT.

entra.notes: Microsoft Learn tutorial for the Atlassian Cloud gallery app; prerequisites still say Atlassian Access.

google.notes: Atlassian runs its own Google Workspace user sync; Google Marketplace page not checked.

onelogin.notes: From Atlassian's own provisioning guide list; OneLogin catalogue page not loaded.

jumpcloud.notes: From Atlassian's own provisioning guide list; JumpCloud catalogue page not loaded.

fallbacks.other_sync: Atlassian-run Google Workspace user sync; Azure AD nested-group sync
fallbacks.notes: Okta's Trello app mentions JIT, but no Atlassian page confirms JIT for Trello.
